newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 10.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The crown strengthened yesterday. After starting at 10.2 percent below its former central parity, it reached 8.2 percent below central parity during the course of the day.
- Consumer prices increased in May by 0.1 percent month-on-month, compared to 6.3 percent in May 1996, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau.
- Industrial production increased by 6.l3 percent, and construction by 5.9 percent year-on-year in April.
- According to a credible source from the central bank, the two remaining candidates in the tender for Agrobanka are ING Bank and General Electric.
- After this year's harvest, millers predict prices of their products will increase by seven to eight percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Only a few weeks until the Madrid summit, which will decide on the entry of the Czech Republic into NATO, more than half of all Czechs are in favour of NATO membership, while this was only 39.9 percent two months ago.
- Ceskomoravske Doly obtained a majority stake in the former foreign trade company Metalimex. Together with its subsidiary, Ceskomoravske Doly now owns 51 percent of shares of Metalimex.
- Yesterday, Chemapol Group signed a contract for a $60 million dollar credit from Credit Lyonnais, with interest of 0.625 percent above the interbank rate LIBOR.

- After a meeting yesterday of the Czech-Slovak customs union, now led by Czech Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl, Slovak Economic Minister Karol Cesnek said the decision to introduce an import quota on Czech beer is final and further quotas may be required to restrict imports of other items. Kuhnl said they do not plan to cancel the union.
PRAVO - Parliament will debate a confidence vote on Tuesday.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus refused more support for science from the government budget. He said, "Science will never have the social position it had under communism."

LIDOVE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said to representatives of the conservative European Democratic Union, who will meet today in Prague, that the primary causes of high unemployment are restrictive social programmes.
- For the first four months of this year, 29.8 million foreigners visited the Czech Republic, a year-on-year increase of 3.3 percent.

- Representatives of the pipe-making companies troubled with the announcement from the EU of an antidumping charge will meet with the Industry and Trade Ministry today before they meet with the European Commission of the EU next week.
